analysis.title: Walmart Inc. (WMT): Share gains continued across categories, supported by price investment; FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: Walmart closed down 1.0% (vs. S&P 500 at -2.0%) after a 3Q earnings beat and a raise to 2026 guidance.

Walmart US comp of +2.9% was in line with consensus (FactSet) and accelerated from +2.6% in 2Q. It was driven by traffic (+1.5%) and average ticket (+1.4%), including a ~70 bps net headwind from pharmacy deflation.
Price investments led to share gains, particularly in grocery, where the company saw some of the highest share gains in three years. Walmart US grocery comps were up mid-single digits.
3Q operating income was $7,770mn with a 4.1% margin, above consensus at 4.0%. Global operating income (cc) grew 5.5% y/y, above 3Q guidance of +2.0-4.0% and ahead of sales (cc) at +4.4%.
eCommerce sales were up 23% with nearly 50% growth in marketplace sales. Walmart US general merchandise GMV grew mid-single digits, above the low-single-digit reported comp for the category.
Management called the consumer stable and resilient, with some pressure earlier this year in April and June.

Walmart US had ~7.7K rollbacks at the end of 3Q, above the ~5.0-5.5K average, and the count is returning toward historical levels. Management plans to keep prices as low as possible for as long as possible, while noting cost pressure in fuel and transportation.
Walmart used tariff refunds to grow market share and set up continued share gains in 2H.

2026 guidance: net sales growth (cc) of +4.9-5.2%, up from +4.0-5.0% prior (vs. consensus +5.6%). Adj. operating income growth (cc) of +8.0-8.6%, up from +7.0-8.5%. Adj. EPS of $2.84-2.89, up from $2.80-2.87 (vs. consensus $2.89).
Implied 4Q guidance: net sales growth (cc) of +4.5-5.5% (vs. consensus +5.0%), adj. operating income growth (cc) of +4.0-6.0% and adj. EPS of $0.73-0.78 (vs. consensus $0.78).

Maximum Fair Pricing is expected to be a ~125 bp headwind to the Walmart US comp, partly offset by a ~50 bps tailwind from GLP-1, both unchanged from the prior guide. Flipkart's BBD event timing is expected to add ~100 bps to 4Q sales growth.

Management expects a strong holiday season. Back-to-school and Halloween both went well, and Walmart has historically treated back-to-school as an early indicator of holiday performance. Marketplace inventory has been forward-deployed into a couple hundred stores.
GS sees conservatism in the 2026 guidance given macro uncertainty and expects share gains to continue through the rest of the year.

GS reiterates Buy with the 12-month price target raised to $134 from $132, implying 6.3% upside from $126.04. The new target uses relative P/E multiples of 210%/215%/220% (vs. 160%/165%/170% prior) and a lower market multiple of 17.3x (vs. 22.8x prior).
GS estimate changes: 4Q26 EPS unchanged at $0.79, 2026 EPS to $2.91 from $2.90, 2027 EPS to $3.19 from $3.21, 2028 EPS to $3.65 from $3.66. A 2029 EPS estimate of $4.16 is introduced.

market_movers.rationale: Share gains from price investment, a raised 2026 guide that GS views as conservative, and improving profitability support earnings growth into 2027. The price target rose to $134 from $132.

earnings_insights: WMT 3Q26 reported: Walmart US comp +2.9% (in line with FactSet consensus), operating income $7,770mn, 4.1% margin vs. consensus 4.0%. Global operating income (cc) +5.5% y/y vs. guidance of +2.0-4.0%.
WMT raised 2026 guidance. Adj. EPS is $2.84-2.89 (prior $2.80-2.87, consensus $2.89). Net sales growth (cc) is +4.9-5.2% (consensus +5.6%). Adj. operating income growth (cc) is +8.0-8.6%.
WMT implied 4Q26 guidance: adj. EPS $0.73-0.78 (consensus $0.78), net sales growth (cc) +4.5-5.5% (consensus +5.0%), adj. operating income growth (cc) +4.0-6.0%.

GS estimates: 4Q26E EPS $0.79 (unchanged), 2026E EPS $2.91 (from $2.90), 2027E $3.19 (from $3.21), 2028E $3.65 (from $3.66), 2029E $4.16 (new). 2026E net revenue growth +5.9% (from +5.6%) and gross margin 24.6% (from 24.5%).
risk_factors: Inability to use expense leverage to offset investments in e-commerce and pricing.
Pressure from wages or transportation costs, including fuel.
Maximum Fair Pricing headwind of ~125 bp to the Walmart US comp.
